subject: Acme Analytics — data-scrub request (prompts/outputs/logs) and confirmation
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.example>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data-scrub request: prompts/outputs/logs for account ACME-2197

Hi Hannah,

We have a regulatory obligation in the EU to permanently remove a subset of customer interaction data tied to a now-deleted project (ACME-2197). The items to be removed are:
- user prompts and generated outputs (text) related to that project
- short-term KV cache and any persisted intermediate outputs
- request/response logs for the date range 2025-11-01 to 2026-06-30

Please confirm Redwood's standard workflow for:
1) identifying and enumerating matching artifacts across regions and storage backends,
2) executing the deletion (what systems are involved),
3) producing a machine-readable "deletion manifest" that lists objects removed, and
4) a human-readable confirmation letter we can file with our DPA.

We also need an estimated timeline and whether you can provide an audit link (immutable log or signed statement) once deletion is complete. If you need a signed attestation from us before we proceed, let us know.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Security Operations
Acme Analytics

--
Attachment: request_scope_ACME-2197.pdf (application/pdf, stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.example>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>

Subject: Re: Data-scrub request: prompts/outputs/logs for account ACME-2197

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear scope. We're able to handle this; I want to confirm a few details and propose the steps/timeline below so Acme can align internal approvals.

Scope confirmation (please reply to confirm):
- Confirm that the scope is all artifacts tagged project:ACME-2197 across EU region only (yes/no).
- Confirm whether you want us to also remove any archived snapshots older than 90 days in the global backups (this is an extra step that requires a separate approval).

Proposed workflow (high level):
1) Verify identifiers and produce a pre-delete inventory (JSON/CSV manifest) listing object keys, S3 paths, and internal request ids.
2) Run a scoped delete job (read-once) that removes prompts/outputs, request logs, and intermediate KV cache entries; API logs that are fed into long-term analytics will be redacted rather than deleted unless you request full removal (see backups note).
3) Generate a deletion_manifest_v1.csv and post a signed audit snapshot to a Drive folder; provide a signed attestation PDF for your records.
4) Re-run a verification pass 72 hours after deletion to confirm objects are not recoverable via standard tooling; we will include hash digests in the manifest.

Estimated timeline: pre-delete inventory within 48 hours after you confirm scope; deletion window 2–3 business days after inventory sign-off and any legal attestation. Total: ~5 business days typical if scope is limited to EU region.

I’ve looped in Dev (engineering) for technical steps and Marissa (CS) to help coordinate attestation and delivery.

If that plan works, reply with scope confirmations and any specific compliance language you need in the attestation.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

--
(Notice: we treat deletion requests as actioned only after customer confirmation of scope.)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data-scrub request: prompts/outputs/logs for account ACME-2197

Thanks — a few technical notes to set expectations and list artifacts we'll produce:

Technical checklist (engineering):
- Inventory: we'll export a CSV with columns [object_key, storage_backend, region, created_at, content_hash]. Typical backends: EU-S3, EU-archive (glacier-type), and internal KV-store (sharded).
- Delete job: we run a one-way deletion job per backend with job ids; for S3-like stores we use delete markers + immediate removal for objects in the customer-managed EU buckets; for on-prem snapshots in the EU cluster we run the scrub utility (scrub-eu --project ACME-2197).
- Backups: global backups taken as weekly snapshots are retained for disaster recovery. We can schedule secure removal from backups on request but that requires a longer retention gating (we will need your signed attestation to proceed).
- Logs: API request logs that have been ingested into analytics pipelines will be purged from the ingestion layer and redacted at the analytics store; raw ingestion archives (if any) will be included in the manifest.

Attachments: I’m attaching a draft deletion_manifest_v1.csv with a sample row and the expected column schema. This is a stub — final manifest will include object hashes and job ids.

Estimated time: inventory export ~24–36 hours once scope confirmed; actual delete run ~4–8 hours per backend; verification pass after 72 hours.

Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference

Confirmed scope: EU region only; project tag ACME-2197. We do NOT request removal from global weekly backups at this time. Please proceed with the workflow you outlined.

We need the human-readable confirmation letter to include the following clause verbatim for regulatory filing: 
"Redwood Inference certifies that the items enumerated in deletion_manifest_v1.csv associated with project ACME-2197 have been permanently removed from production storage and are not recoverable via standard restore procedures as of the deletion date."

Please also include a link to the audit folder and a signed attestation (PDF). We can sign a short Docusign envelope verifying we received the attestation after deletion completes.

Regards,

Hannah Schmitt
